title: ALMA Observations of Peculiar Embedded Icy Objects
question: What is the physical and chemical nature of two peculiar isolated infrared objects with deep ice and dust absorption features discovered by AKARI?

data.arrays: 12 m main array (45 antennas) and 7 m Morita array / ACA (10 antennas)
data.sensitivity: 0.04-0.05 K in CO and SiO line cubes; ~0.1 mJy/beam (1 sigma) in continuum

what.value: Infrared positions, photometric SEDs, K_S-band magnitudes, and peak optical depths of 9.7 um silicate dust (2.9 +/- 0.3) and 3.0 um H2O ice (4.5 +/- 0.5) absorption features for Object 1 and 2

evidence.quote: Positions of the infrared point-sources measured by AKARI are RA = 14$^\mathrm{h}$4$^\mathrm{m}$13.2s and Dec = -61$\ensuremath{^\circ}$12$\ensuremath{'}$40.1$''$ for Object 1 and RA = 14$^\mathrm{h}$4$^\mathrm{m}$20.2s and Dec = -61$\ensuremath{^\circ}$15$\ensuremath{'}$49.5$''$ for Object 2 (IRCS), respectively.

evidence.loc: Gas column densities and constraint on the source size
evidence.quote: First, we estimate $N_{\mathrm{H_2}}$ by using the peak optical depth of the 9.7 $\mu$m silicate dust absorption ($	au_{\mathrm{9.7}}$) and the 3.0 $\mu$m H$_2$O ice absorption ($	au_{\mathrm{3.0}}$), which are measured to be 2.9 $\pm$ 0.3 and 4.5 $\pm$ 0.5 for Object 1 (cite: Ona21).
cf., the $K_\mathrm{S}$-band magnitudes of Object 1 and 2 are 10.4 and 11.7 mag, respectively (cite: Ona21).

evidence.quote: We estimate kinematic distances to the icy objects and the surrounding gas using the kinematic distance calculator, which is based on the method described in (cite: Rei09) and the Galactic parameters from (cite: Rei14).

recipe.goal: Extract molecular spectra and measure line parameters
recipe.method: Extract spectra from a 0.7'' diameter circular aperture centered at the emission peak and perform Gaussian fitting to derive T_br, FWHM (Delta V), V_LSR, and velocity-integrated intensity
key_parameters: Aperture diameter = 0.7'' centered at emission peak

recipe.goal: Derive CO and SiO column densities and SiO/CO ratios
recipe.method: Calculate total column densities N_CO and N_SiO from integrated intensities using standard optically-thin LTE equations and spectroscopic parameters from CDMS
assumptions: Optically-thin emission under Local Thermodynamic Equilibrium (LTE) with T_rot = 20-50 K (excluding T_rot >= 80 K due to non-detection of hot-core tracers)

recipe.goal: Estimate kinematic distances and bolometric luminosities
recipe.method: Input measured systemic velocities into the Reid et al. (2009, 2014) kinematic distance calculator, then integrate available photometric SED data from 2 to 20 um using the derived distances
assumptions: Objects are co-moving with Galactic rotation; far kinematic distance (9.3 kpc) is adopted for Object 1 based on similarity to Object 2 (13.4 kpc)

recipe.goal: Derive H2 column densities from IR absorption, CO emission, and dust continuum upper limits to constrain source size
recipe.method: Compare N_H2 derived from 9.7 um silicate and 3.0 um H2O ice optical depths with beam-averaged N_H2 from CO(3-2) and 3-sigma 853 um continuum upper limits to infer beam dilution factors and physical source sizes
key_parameters: Beam size = 0.8'' (corresponding to 7400 au at 9.3 kpc and 10700 au at 13.4 kpc)
assumptions: A_V / A_K = 8.8; foreground A_V (104 mag) is doubled for embedded geometry; N_H / (A_B - A_V) = 5.8 x 10^21 cm^-2 mag^-1; R_V = A_V / (A_B - A_V) = 4; all H in H2 giving N_H2 / A_V = 7.3 x 10^20 cm^-2 mag^-1
CO/H2 ratio = 10^-4; dust opacity kappa_nu = 2.14 cm^2 g^-1 at 853 um; dust-to-gas mass ratio Z = 0.008; T_d = 20-50 K
